title: Unramified algebra maps descend along directed colimits
statement: Let $I$ be a nonempty directed set and let $A=\varinjlim_{i\in I}A_i$ be a directed colimit of commutative rings. Fix $i_0\in I$ and a map of $A_{i_0}$-algebras $\varphi_0:B_0\to C_0$. For $i\ge i_0$ put $B_i=A_i\otimes_{A_{i_0}}B_0$, $C_i=A_i\otimes_{A_{i_0}}C_0$, and $B=A\otimes_{A_{i_0}}B_0$, $C=A\otimes_{A_{i_0}}C_0$. Assume that $B\to C$ is unramified as a ring map, meaning that $C$ is a finitely generated $B$-algebra and its module of Kähler differentials $\Omega_{C/B}$ is zero [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials], and assume that $C_0$ is a finitely generated $B_0$-algebra. Then there exists $i\ge i_0$ such that $B_i\to C_i$ is unramified: $C_i$ is finitely generated over $B_i$ and $\Omega_{C_i/B_i}=0$.

proof.text: Choose generators $x_1,\ldots,x_m$ of $C_0$ over $B_0$, with $m=0$ permitted, using [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra]. Put $M_0=\Omega_{C_0/B_0}$ and $v_r=\mathrm d x_r$. Apply [lem-trf-base-changed-algebra-differential-generators] with $T=A_i$ for every $i\ge i_0$, and with $T=A$. Thus the $x_{r,i}=1\otimes x_r$ generate $C_i$ over $B_i$, their differentials generate $\Omega_{C_i/B_i}$, and the $v_r$ generate $M_0$. These applications use exactly the scalar-extended map $\mathrm{id}\otimes\varphi_0$.

source.place: Tag 0C4F (lemma-colimit-unramified), proof: choose algebra generators; tensor expansion

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-outer-base-change-differential-comparison] over $A_{i_0}$, first with $T=A$ and then with each $T=A_i$. It gives isomorphisms $F_T:T\otimes_{A_{i_0}}M_0\simeq\Omega_{C_T/B_T}$ satisfying $F_T(1\otimes v_r)=\mathrm d(1\otimes x_r)$. The unramified hypothesis gives $\Omega_{C/B}=0$, so injectivity of $F_A$ yields $1\otimes v_r=0$ in $A\otimes_{A_{i_0}}M_0$ for every $r$.

source.place: Tag 00RV (lemma-differentials-base-change); Tag 0C4F (lemma-colimit-unramified), vanishing in the colimit

proof.text: Apply clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-directed-colimit-base-change-elementwise] with initial index $i_0$ and the arbitrary $A_{i_0}$-module $M_0$. For each $r$ apply it to $1\otimes v_r\in A_{i_0}\otimes_{A_{i_0}}M_0$: step 2 says its image in $A\otimes_{A_{i_0}}M_0$ is zero. Obtain $j_r\ge i_0$ with $1\otimes v_r=0$ in $A_{j_r}\otimes_{A_{i_0}}M_0$. Choose $i\ge i_0,j_1,\ldots,j_m$ by finitely many applications of directedness (take $i=i_0$ if $m=0$). The transition map sends $a\otimes\omega$ to $\alpha_{i j_r}(a)\otimes\omega$, so it sends these zero elements to $1\otimes v_r=0$ in $A_i\otimes_{A_{i_0}}M_0$. Applying $F_{A_i}$ from step 2 yields $\mathrm d x_{r,i}=0$ for every $r$.

source.place: Tag 0C4F (lemma-colimit-unramified), final sentence; Tags 00D7 (lemma-zero-directed-limit) and 00DD (lemma-tensor-products-commute-with-limits) for the existing elementwise tensor-colimit lemma

proof.text: At the index $i$ of step 3, every $\mathrm d x_{r,i}$ is zero. Since step 1 says these elements generate $\Omega_{C_i/B_i}$, every element of that module is a linear combination of zero elements; hence it is zero. Step 1 also supplies algebra generators for $C_i$ over $B_i$. These are exactly the two unramified conditions in the unchanged statement, and $i\ge i_0$. If $m=0$, step 3 takes $i=i_0$.

lean.statement: theorem exists_unramified_stage_of_colimit {I : Type u} [Preorder I] [IsDirected I (· ≤ ·)] [Nonempty I] (F : I ⥤ CommRingCat.{u}) [HasColimit F] (i₀ : I) (B₀ : Type v) (C₀ : Type w) [CommRing B₀] [CommRing C₀] [Algebra (F.obj i₀) B₀] [Algebra (F.obj i₀) C₀] (φ₀ : B₀ →ₐ[F.obj i₀] C₀) (hfg : φ₀.toRingHom.FiniteType) (hunramified : letI : Algebra (F.obj i₀) ↥(colimit F) := (colimit.ι F i₀).hom.toAlgebra (Algebra.TensorProduct.map (AlgHom.id (F.obj i₀) ↥(colimit F)) φ₀).toRingHom.FiniteType ∧ Subsingleton (@KaehlerDifferential (↥(colimit F) ⊗[F.obj i₀] B₀) (↥(colimit F) ⊗[F.obj i₀] C₀) _ _ (Algebra.TensorProduct.map (AlgHom.id (F.obj i₀) ↥(colimit F)) φ₀).toRingHom.toAlgebra)) : ∃ (i : I) (h : i₀ ≤ i), letI : Algebra (F.obj i₀) (F.obj i) := (F.map (homOfLE h)).hom.toAlgebra (Algebra.TensorProduct.map (AlgHom.id (F.obj i₀) (F.obj i)) φ₀).toRingHom.FiniteType ∧ Subsingleton (@KaehlerDifferential ((F.obj i) ⊗[F.obj i₀] B₀) ((F.obj i) ⊗[F.obj i₀] C₀) _ _ (Algebra.TensorProduct.map (AlgHom.id (F.obj i₀) (F.obj i)) φ₀).toRingHom.toAlgebra)
